nodes.label: Old Habits Die Hard: How Conversational History Geometrically Traps LLMs
nodes.author: Adi Simhi, Fazl Barez, Martin Tutek, Yonatan Belinkov, Shay B. Cohen
nodes.rationale: Introduces HISTORY-ECHOES framework analyzing how LLM behavior persists across conversational turns through probabilistic (Markov chain) and geometric (latent space) perspectives. Demonstrates carryover effects are structural features encoded in model representations.

nodes.label: HISTORY-ECHOES Framework
nodes.rationale: Dual-perspective framework for analyzing behavioral persistence in LLMs. Bridges probabilistic (Markov chain trace) and geometric (latent space angles) analyses to reveal how conversational history creates structural constraints on model behavior.

nodes.label: Geometric Trap in Latent Space
nodes.rationale: Key finding: behavioral persistence manifests as geometric separation in latent space. Large angular separation between phenomenon states makes transitions incomplete, trapping model in previous behavioral state.

nodes.label: Markov Chain Analysis of LLM Behavior
nodes.rationale: Models conversational dynamics as first-order Markov chain with binary states (phenomenon present/absent). Trace of transition matrix quantifies state persistence; values >1 indicate carryover effects.

nodes.label: Carryover Effects Across Phenomena
nodes.rationale: Empirical finding: refusal exhibits strongest carryover effects, followed by sycophancy, with hallucination weakest. Suggests phenomena vary in coherence within model representations.

nodes.label: Topic Coherence Dependency of Carryover
nodes.rationale: Carryover effects dissolve in topically inconsistent conversations. Suggests behavioral persistence is context-dependent, with implications for adversarial jailbreaking strategies.

nodes.label: Hidden State Geometry Analysis
nodes.rationale: Constructs orthogonal bases from phenomenon-present and phenomenon-absent activations. Measures angular separation (θref) and transition angles to quantify geometric constraints on behavior.

nodes.label: Gram-Schmidt Basis Construction
nodes.rationale: Method for constructing orthonormal basis from mean hidden states of phenomenon classes. Enables projection of hidden states onto 2D subspace for angular analysis.

nodes.label: Orthogonal Procrustes Rotation Analysis
nodes.rationale: Estimates optimal rotation angles characterizing state transitions. Reveals incomplete rotations between phenomenon states, providing evidence of geometric trapping.

nodes.label: Markov Chain Mixing Time Analysis
nodes.rationale: Analyzes convergence rate of Markov chain via second eigenvalue. Refusal exhibits slowest mixing (highest persistence), hallucination fastest, indicating phenomenon-specific structural properties.

nodes.label: Higher-Order Markov Chain Analysis
nodes.rationale: Evaluates whether phenomena depend on more than one previous turn. Finds first-order history dominates but second/third-order dependencies remain non-negligible.

nodes.label: Layer Depth and Geometric Correlation
nodes.rationale: Strongest correlation between probabilistic and geometric perspectives at 85% relative depth (upper-middle layers). Aligns with prior findings on optimal layers for semantic concept detection.

nodes.label: Conditioned Effect on Prior State
nodes.rationale: Holds question fixed while varying preceding state. Demonstrates model responses shift as function of prior state, providing direct evidence that previous states shape current behavior.

nodes.label: Closed Model Inference via Probabilistic Perspective
nodes.rationale: Probabilistic perspective applicable to closed models (GPT-5, Claude-Opus-4.5) without white-box access. Enables inference of internal geometric traps from external behavior patterns.
